Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back. The players are out in the middle for the chase. Hasini Perera and Vishmi Gunarathne to open for Sri Lanka Women. It will be Kashvee Gautam with the ball for India Women. Here we go!
…THE RUN CHASE…

Sri Lanka Women were decent with the ball but gave away plenty of loose balls at regular intervals, that was capitalized by the Women in Blue. Chamari Athapaththu and Sugandika Kumari were the pick of the bowlers with three wickets each, while Inoka Ranaweera and Dewmi Vihanga snapped one apiece. Sri Lanka Women failed to go past 150 in their most recent outing against India Women but will need to bat much better today if they are to chase this formidable score. Join us back in a while for Sri Lanka Women's reply.

Another impressive batting effort from India Women helps them post an excellent score of 275/9 from their 50 overs. Having been sent into bat first, India Women lost Smriti Mandhana early, but Pratika Rawal, Harleen Deol, Harmanpreet Kaur, and Jemimah Rodrigues played handy knocks and kept the scoreboard ticking. Richa Ghosh smashed a quick-fire fifty to up the tempo, and some lusty blows by the lower order batters took India Women past the 270-run mark. India Women were on course to breach 300 but lost wickets at the wrong time and had to settle for 275.

The Women's Tri-Series in Sri Lanka continues with the second round of fixtures coming your way. It will be hosts, Sri Lanka Women taking on an in-form India Women side at the R. Premadasa Stadium in Colombo, Sri Lanka. India Women dominated the first round of fixtures as they brushed aside both Sri Lanka Women and South Africa Women and they now have a chance to storm straight into the Final with a win. Sri Lanka Women, on the other hand, rallied back from their shoddy outing with the bat against India to overcome South Africa and can now go level on points with India if they are to avenge their previous defeat and the home crowd will definitely give them that added inspiration. Talking a bit more about the hosts, they were completely dismantled by the Indian spinners in the opening game of the series but Hasini Perera, Harshitha Samarawickrama and Kavisha Dilhari all managed to bounce back against the Proteas and close the gap of India Women. Sri Lanka Women do have a well-balanced bowling attack as well but they need their skipper, Chamari Athapaththu, to fire with the bat up top if they are to have any chance of stopping this Indian side. Speaking of the Indian side, they had a much tougher outing against South Africa Women in their previous game, but in a high-scoring contest, they managed to hold their nerves with the ball and remained unbeaten. Pratika Rawal has been the standout with two fifties in as many matches and that top 3 has seemed so dominant. Also, when their middle order was required, the likes of Harleen Deol, Jemimah Rodrigues and Richa Ghosh all made valuable contributions. The spin attack has been working wonders and a rejuvenated Sneh Rana seems to be flourishing in the ODI format. She took a five-wicket haul against the Proteas, including the all-important wicket of centurion Tazmin Brits and that eventually made the difference. Now then, will the Indian spinners dominate the Lankan batters again? Or will Chamari Athapaththu lead from the front and turn the tables on India? We shall find out in due time.
